definitions.explanation: Used in conversation to express strong agreement or to confirm what someone has said. Often signals that the speaker has just remembered or recognized something.

examples.japanese: そうそう、⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧だ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
「⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧？」「そうそう、⟦{驚|おどろ}いた→驚く：01255_odoroku⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。」
examples.english: "Did you see yesterday's news?" "Yeah, I was surprised."

examples.japanese: そうそう、⟦{言|い}い→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{忘|わす}れ→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧てた⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、⟦{来週|らいしゅう}→来週：00746_raishuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わった→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: Oh right, I forgot to mention — next week's plans have changed.

notes:
FUNCTIONS:
- Agreement: enthusiastically confirms what someone just said, stronger than a single そう. Often used while nodding along. 「⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧おいしい⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧」「そうそう！」
- Recollection: introduces something the speaker just remembered, like "oh right" or "that reminds me." そうそう、⟦{言|い}い→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{忘|わす}れ→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧てた⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧… (Oh right, I forgot to mention…)

WATCH OUT:
そうそう followed by a negative is a different word, an adverb meaning "not that often, not so easily": ⟦こんな→こんな：02881_konna⟧⟦チャンス→チャンス：03857_chansu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧そうそう⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (A chance like this doesn't come often).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- そうだ⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: agreement (neutral)
- そうです⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: agreement (polite)
- ⟦そういえば→そういえば：27571_souieba⟧: speaking of which, come to think of it
- あ、そうだ: oh, that's right (sudden recollection)

REGISTER:
Casual. In polite or formal conversation, そうです⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ is preferred. Very common in speech, rare in formal writing.

cross_references.label: speaking of which, come to think of it
